description: A model that grants or denies access based on attributes of the user, resource, action, and environment against defined policies.

A major email attack threat in which an attacker impersonates a trusted person to trick someone into transferring funds, changing payment details, disclosing sensitive data, or taking other unauthorized actions.

The Zscaler cloud’s central control-plane component, which monitors service infrastructure, coordinates authentication, manages ZPA policies, and distributes configuration, software and database updates, and threat intelligence.
A security solution that mediates access between users and cloud services to enforce organizational policies and protect cloud applications and data.
A PCI DSS term for the people, processes, technologies, and system components that store, process, or transmit CHD or SAD, along with components that support their security.
A protected piece of data in the Clark-Wilson integrity model whose accuracy and completeness must be strictly maintained.
A foundational cybersecurity model—Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability—used to guide security controls and assess information—system risks.
A U.S. Department of War cybersecurity certification program that verifies whether defense contractors and subcontractors implement required controls to protect FCI and CUI.
A cybersecurity operating model that continuously identifies attacker-exploitable exposures, prioritizes those that matter most, and drives their remediation.

A hands-on cybersecurity competition where participants solve challenges in areas such as web security, digital forensics, network analysis, and vulnerability exploitation to uncover hidden “flags”—text strings that verify successful completion.
A reference method for publicly known information-security vulnerabilities and exposures.
An open framework for rating the severity of security vulnerabilities in computing systems.

An plant-wide industrial control system that distributes control logic across multiple controllers throughout a manufacturing facility, forming a core OT platform whose compromise can disrupt production, endanger safety, and affect critical infrastructure operations.
Detects the unauthorized transmission or disclosure of sensitive data and prevents its occurrence.
Cybersecurity technology that continuously monitors endpoint devices to detect, investigate, and respond to cyber threats in real time.
The practice of improving visibility, control, and governance of identities, accounts, roles, and access privileges across an organization.

A centrally managed security solution that prevents malware and other threats from compromising endpoint devices through antivirus, behavioral analysis, policy enforcement, and other preventive controls.
Cisco’s secure email gateway, formerly known as ESA, filters inbound and outbound email to block spam, phishing, and malware while providing encryption, DLP, and policy enforcement.
Software installed on endpoint devices that communicates with a central security platform to enforce policies, monitor activity, and help prevent, detect, and respond to threats.

The hardware, software, and networks that monitor and control physical processes in industrial and critical infrastructure environments, where security protects against cyber threats while preserving safety, availability, and reliability.

A security technology that monitors network traffic to detect and automatically block malicious activity in real time by dropping packets, blocking IP addresses, or terminating suspicious connections.
A cybersecurity capability that detects, investigates, and responds to attacks targeting identities, credentials, accounts, and authentication systems.
A security principle that restricts users to the minimum privileges and access needed to perform their authorized tasks.
A cybersecurity service in which a third-party provider continuously monitors an organization's environment to detect threats, investigate suspicious activity, and support incident response.
A security method that requires users to verify their identity with at least two distinct factors—something they know, have, or are—before granting access.
A security framework that verifies users and devices before granting network access, enforcing policies based on identity, device type, location, and security posture.
An endpoint security solution, beyond traditional signature-based detection, that uses behavioral analysis, machine learning, and threat intelligence to detect and block known and unkown threats.
Inspects and controls network traffic, identifies applications, and blocks attacks and exploits.
Hardware and software used to monitor control and automate physical processes in industrial settings.
The practice of securing, controlling, monitoring, and auditing privileged accounts and administrative access to critical systems, applications, and data.
The Zero Trust component that evaluates access requests against security policies and context, then grants, denies, or revokes access.
The Zero Trust component that enforces the PDP’s decisions by allowing, blocking, or terminating access to a resource.
Any information that can identify, distinguish, or trace an individual, alone or combined with other information.

A rugged industrial computer—a core ICS foundational component—used in automation and to monitor inputs from sensors, switches, etc., in order to execute programmed logic, and to control outputs such as motors, valves, and relays in real time.

Commonly refers to the NIST Risk Management Framework, a structured process for identifying, assessing, mitigating, and continuously monitoring security and privacy risks throughout a system’s lifecycle.

As a wide area solution, it comprises the hardware, software, and networks used for centralized monitoring and control of geographically distributed industrial processes through data collection, alarms, and supervisory commands, with security focused on preserving safety, availability, and reliability.
An email security solution that inspects inbound and outbound messages to detect threats and enforce organizational policies.
A Cisco Splunk security platform that automates and coordinates incident investigation and response across multiple tools using predefined workflows called playbooks.
A dedicated site and centralized team that monitors, detects, investigates, and responds to cybersecurity threats across an organization’s IT environment.

A cloud-delivered Cisco Systems security architecture that integrates multiple security controls into a unified service to secure user access to applications, internet resources, and data from anywhere.
A Cisco Systems on-premises web security appliance that provides SWG capabilities to inspect, filter, and control web traffic.
A security capability that inspects, filters, and controls web traffic to protect users and prevent malware, phishing, access to malicious websites, data loss, and other web threats.
The continuous process of detecting, investigating, containing, and remediating cyber threats to minimize their organizational impact.
An authorized procedure in the Clark-Wilson integrity model that operates on CDIs or converts approved UDI into valid CDI.
Represents data that has not been validated against the Clark–Wilson integrity model’s constraints, such as arbitrary user input.
Cisco’s previous SWG, now called SWA, provides URL filtering, malware protection, web traffic inspection, and policy enforcement to protect users from internet threats.
A certificate standard that defines the format of public-key certificates used to authenticate identities and support encryption, digital signatures, and secure communications.
A cybersecurity platform that collects, correlates, and analyzes security data from multiple sources to detect and respond to threats across an organization’s environment.
A lightweight endpoint agent that connects users’ devices to Zscaler services for secure access to destinations from any location.
A cloud-based digital experience monitoring service that measures user, device, network, and application performance to pinpoint the causes of user-experience issues.
An inline security gateway service that applies security and organizational policies to traffic before it reaches its destination.
Provides access to specific private applications without placing users on the corporate network, offering an alternative to VPN-based remote access.
A CISA framework that helps organizations assess and improve their adoption of Zero Trust Architecture.
Only grants access to authorized applications and resources through continuous verification of user identity, device, and context, following the Zero Trust principle: "Never trust, always verify."
